text:
sophia: Heads-up: seeing steady GPU memory growth on long-context traces. suspect kv cache reuse across requests is suboptimal when session keys rotate frequently. stats attached from last run.

josh: hmm, can you paste the profiler snippet? is this before or after the recent batching change? :eyes:

sophia: before. main symptoms: slow decline in live KV entries, lots of small evictions, and page faults in the runtime allocator. repro with long conversation (50-80k tokens).

rahul: that sounds like fragmentation + eviction churn. are we TTL-ing per-session keys? if sessions get new IDs on each reconnect we lose reuse.

sophia: we do a short TTL (5m) and also include a per-connection nonce in the cache key. was trying to avoid cross-session leakage, but it's killing reuse.

maria: strong +1 to revisiting key design. maybe split auth-scoped namespace from prompt-prefix key. keep a stable prefix-id that survives reconnects.

josh: quick experiment idea: keep stable `prefix_id = hash(user_id || canonicalized_prompt[:N])` and then combine with short-lived `session_flag` for privacy. that keeps reuse while still allowing invalidation.

rahul: agree. also recommend recording these counters per-prefix: `cache_hits`, `cache_misses`, `evictions`, `avg_entry_size`, `last_access_ts`. we can add a small probe to the runtime to emit those as tags.

perf-bot: profiling summary (run id 2026-03-16T14:02Z):
```
kernel_time_ms: 4120
kv_lookup_time_ms: 710
allocator_page_faults: 132
avg_kv_entry_size_bytes: 2048
eviction_ops: 284
```

sophia: nice. notice kv_lookup_time is non-trivial vs kernel_time. reuse would save both lookup and recompute on kernel path.

josh: on eviction policy: LRU across entire pool is noisy for mixed-length sessions. consider size-aware eviction (LRU-2 with size weighting) or segregated cold pool for very large prefix entries.

maria: any perf regressions after recent batching heuristics change? batching could increase cache lifetime variance if requests are delayed and KV entries get scanned more.

rahul: we ran A/B yesterday: batching v2 increases average batch latency but reduces tokens-per-second cost. no direct KV regression observed in short runs, but long-context runs show more fragmentation. suspect interleaving of long and short sessions in same shard.

josh: action items: 1) add stable `prefix_id` canonicalizer (N=256 chars) 2) enable per-prefix counters in runtime 3) prototype size-aware eviction and segregated pools 4) run long-context repro for 24h with perf probes.

maria: I'll own 1 and 2. will add counters as lightweight atomics and expose via console traces.

rahul: I'll take 3 and run the 24h job. can we tag the repro traffic so we can filter metrics?

sophia: tagging sounds good. test tag `kv-reuse-experiment-2026-03-17`. please post results in this thread.

josh: minor note on key canonicalization: strip ephemeral tokens, normalize whitespace, and limit prompt window. example key: `sha256(user||norm_prompt[:4096])::flags` — keep everything deterministic.

perf-bot: scheduled job: long-context run assigned to rahul, duration 24h, start 2026-03-17T02:00Z. monitor id: LR-7834.

maria: starting a PR for canonicalizer and counters, will ping for review when ready. :rocket:
